messages:
sasha: heads-up — seeing a pretty bad token surge for org-acme in us-west. rpm stayed near limit but tpm exploded and they started getting 429s. looks like a background worker batched lots of prompts. can we discuss smoothing vs hard caps?

omar: can you share the spike shape? is this high QPS or long responses (= tokens/request)?

sasha: here’s a quick summary: 8k requests over ~3m window, avg tokens/request jumped from ~80 to ~400. current per-org policy: rpm=600, tpm=12000, concurrency=30.

lee: that matches TPM being the choke point. long requests multiply token usage. options: sliding token window, token-bucket refill, or keep fixed TPM but raise burst reserve.

kelly: from UX POV i prefer smoothing w/ explicit burst reserve exposed in console. show "burst remaining" + reason: TPM vs RPM vs CONC. customers should see why they hit limits.

omar: implementation note: our counters are redis fixed-window right now (1m TTL). sliding window requires storing per-request timestamps (sorted set) which is heavier. token-bucket is cheaper: keep (tokens, last_refill_ts) per org. pseudo: 
```
policy = {rpm:600, tpm:12000, burst_tokens:30000, refill_rate_tokens_per_sec:200}
if tokens >= req_tokens: allow else throttle
```

lee: token-bucket covers bursts nicely but we still need concurrency cap to prevent many simultaneous large responses tying up GPU. also need to account for tokens consumed by streaming responses (incrementally charge).

deploy-bot: rate-limit-config-service: pushed branch "token-burst-smoothing" -> staging. canary flag: tag=canary-burst (5% traffic).

product-ops: @sasha for console copy: show metric code (RPM|TPM|CONC), current window (1m/5m), burst remaining, and link to "request more capacity". also surface top prompts causing token hits.

omar: another idea: soft-warning header for clients while reserve exists, e.g. X-RateLimit-Warning: "token-burst-active" so smart clients can slow down before 429. then hard 429 when reserve is gone.

kelly: agree. that reduces retry storms. also add telemetry tags: org_id, throttle_reason, tokens_consumed, spike_session_id so we can correlate in dashboards.

lee: perf note: sorted set sliding windows give better accuracy but scale cost. token-bucket + periodic background cleanup is our sweet spot. we'll need prometheus gauges for per-org reserve and histograms for token-consumption-per-request.

kelly: action items:
- omar: prototype token-bucket + streaming charge handling (PR)
- deploy-bot: run canary, surface canary metrics in console
- product-ops: mockup throttle tile + wording
- sasha: attach acme logs + open tracking ticket
ETA: 1 week to staging.

sasha: ok thanks everyone — i'll file the ticket and cc support. :thumbsup:
